questions.question: Which statement about an abstract class in Java is true?
options: It cannot be instantiated with new
All its methods must be abstract
questions.explanation: An abstract class blocks direct object creation, but it can still have constructors, fields and complete methods.

questions.question: Why does this fail to compile? abstract class Fare { abstract int base() { return 10; } }
options: An abstract class needs a constructor
An abstract method cannot have a body
int is not allowed as a return type
questions.explanation: An abstract method ends with a semicolon. Giving it a body contradicts the abstract modifier.

questions.question: What prints? abstract class A { A() { System.out.print("A"); } } class B extends A { B() { System.out.print("B"); } } ... new B();
questions.explanation: The abstract parent constructor runs first through the implicit super() call, then the child constructor.

questions.question: A class has one abstract method. What must be true about the class?
options: It must have a main method
questions.explanation: Any class that contains an abstract method has to be marked abstract itself.

questions.question: abstract class Tax { abstract double rate(); } class Gst extends Tax { } Why does Gst fail to compile?
options: It does not implement rate() and is not abstract
A class cannot extend an abstract class
questions.explanation: A concrete child must implement every inherited abstract method, or be declared abstract too.

questions.question: Which modifier combination is legal on a method?
questions.explanation: protected abstract is fine. final, static and private all prevent overriding, so they cannot pair with abstract.

questions.question: abstract class Fee { int total() { return 2 * unit(); } abstract int unit(); } class Gym extends Fee { int unit() { return 300; } } What does new Gym().total() return?
questions.explanation: total() is inherited from the parent and calls the child's unit(), so it returns 2 * 300 = 600.

questions.question: How many abstract classes can one Java class extend directly?
questions.explanation: Java allows single class inheritance, so a class extends at most one class, abstract or not.

questions.question: In the template method pattern, why is the template method often marked final?
options: So children cannot change the order of work
So it can be called without an object
questions.explanation: final stops subclasses from overriding the method that fixes the sequence, while they still fill in the abstract pieces.

questions.question: abstract class Ticket { } ... Ticket t = new Ticket(); What happens?
questions.explanation: Even without abstract methods, an abstract class cannot be instantiated with new.
